clue.text: Good time on Space Commission

indicators.note: in an across clue 'on' places the following pieces after the one before

parts.note: an en is a printer's space, half an em
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: A good moment for a space agency to get its funding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Space' is the printer's unit EN, not outer space.
explanation.definitionFit: To engage someone is to hire them, just as you commission an artist or builder.

clue.text: Half a month left — ultimately must pay for freshness

indicators.note: Half takes the first half of the eight-letter month's name

parts.note: November is a month

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of each of the next two words

explanation.surface: Mid-month, someone left with bills to settle hopes for something new.
explanation.definitionFit: Novelty is the quality of being new and original, which is freshness.

clue.text: Bridge players support their opponents after ace barely used

indicators.note: after says the rest follows the ace's letter
in a down clue the supporting pair sits underneath the pair it holds up

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for ace on playing cards
East and West sit against South and North at the bridge table
East and West form one partnership in bridge

explanation.surface: A bridge partnership helps out the other side once an ace is played.
explanation.walkthrough: A bridge table has partnerships North-South and East-West; in this down clue EW props up SN from below.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods sold as new have hardly been handled, so they are barely used.

clue.text: Attention: boat swallowed by sea will be set aside

parts.note: to give someone your ear is to give them attention

indicators.note: swallowed by says the boat goes inside the sea

parts.note: the Med is the Mediterranean Sea
an ark is a boat, as in Noah's

explanation.surface: A warning that a boat sunk by the sea will be abandoned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will be' just links the wordplay to the past participle.
explanation.definitionFit: Earmarked funds are reserved for a particular purpose, set aside for it.

clue.text: Modelling work comes first for rival

indicators.note: comes first says the work's letters go before the modelling

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a work
a model is posing

explanation.surface: A model puts the job before everything else.
explanation.definitionFit: Opposing sides are rival ones, set against each other.

clue.text: Painting drum to make waterproof

parts.note: an oil is a painting in oils
a drum skin is the membrane struck by the player

explanation.surface: Coating a drum with paint to keep the rain off it.
explanation.definitionFit: An oilskin is a waterproof garment, a waterproof being a coat that keeps rain out.

clue.text: Something easy about question causes resentment

indicators.note: about says the easy thing goes round the question

parts.note: something easy is as easy as pie, so pie

explanation.surface: Being asked an easy question leaves someone feeling patronised.
explanation.definitionFit: Pique is a fit of irritation from wounded pride, a form of resentment.

clue.text: Irrational number turned up in complicated maths test, discovered crew

indicators.note: in places the upturned number inside the jumbled letters
complicated says the letters of maths are mixed up
turned up in a down clue means read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: pi is the best-known irrational number

indicators.note: discovered means the cover, the outer letters, is taken off test

explanation.surface: An irrational number appears in a tough maths exam.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'turned up' reverses the number; 'complicated' scrambles maths into SHMAT, and 'discovered' takes the cover off test rather than meaning found.
explanation.definitionFit: Shipmates are fellow sailors on one vessel, the crew.

clue.text: In conversation, understand rag editor used shorthand

indicators.note: In conversation says the words are heard spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: understand is know, rag is tat, editor is ed

explanation.surface: A rag's editor, chatting, takes notes in shorthand.
explanation.walkthrough: KNOW + TAT + ED, spoken, matches the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Shorthand is a system of notation, so writing in it is notating.

clue.text: Loose quilt cover isn't scratching child's head — one with a dummy

indicators.note: loose says the letters are freed to rearrange
scratching means the child's initial is struck out of cover
head points to the first letter of child's

explanation.surface: A loose quilt cover stops a child scratching its head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scratching' removes C from cover to leave OVER; QUILT + OVER + ISNT is rearranged by 'Loose'.
explanation.definitionFit: A ventriloquist performs with a dummy whose voice they throw.

clue.text: Repercussions from football team visiting bar

indicators.note: visiting says the team goes inside the bar

parts.note: to bar is to block
WBA is West Bromwich Albion, an English football club

explanation.surface: Trouble follows a football team's trip to the pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Blowback is the unintended adverse consequences of an action, its repercussions.

clue.text: Content to leave education — American university, Yale's heading for feud

indicators.note: content to leave says the inside of education is dropped, keeping its ends

parts.note: MIT is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology

indicators.note: heading points to the first letter of Yale's

explanation.surface: A student happy to quit their American university, Yale, in a dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Content' looks like happy but means the contents of education.
explanation.definitionFit: Enmity is mutual hostility, the bitter feeling behind a feud.

clue.text: and 15 Down Somehow make reservation with Youth Hostel in new town after cycling to reach castle

indicators.note: in places the hostel inside the booking

parts.note: to book is to make a reservation
YH is the abbreviation for Youth Hostel

indicators.note: after cycling says the town's first letter moves to its end

parts.note: Corby is a new town in Northamptonshire, England, built after the Second World War
the castle in chess is also called a rook

explanation.surface: Booking a youth hostel in a new town, then cycling on to a castle.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something by hook or by crook means achieving it somehow, by any means available.

clue.text: Honour doctor as nice show of respect

parts.note: the OBE is a British honour, Officer of the Order of the British Empire

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters are altered

explanation.surface: A doctor is honoured for being nice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctor' looks like a person but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Obeisance is a bow or other gesture of deference, a show of respect.

clue.text: Literary twelve from revolutionary publication, working for an independent

indicators.note: for says one piece takes the place of the other
revolutionary means turned round, so read backwards

parts.note: an edition is a publication
I is the abbreviation for independent
on means working, as a machine that is on

explanation.surface: Twelve literary works from a radical press, recast for an independent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' gives NOITIDE; working's ON replaces the first I.
explanation.definitionFit: Noontide is a poetic word for midday, twelve o'clock.

clue.text: See 12
Dodge oddly in and out, without cover — initiation to military attachment

indicators.note: in places those letters inside and
oddly takes the first, third and fifth letters of Dodge
without cover means the outer letters of out are removed
initiation to points to the first letter of military

explanation.surface: Dodging in and out without cover during a soldier's first training.
explanation.walkthrough: DDE (odd letters of Dodge) go into AND; out uncovered leaves U.
explanation.definitionFit: An addendum is something added to a document, an attachment.

clue.text: Discuss using a hundred pounds instead of a 'ton' — disaster

indicators.note: instead of says one piece takes the other's place

parts.note: to discuss is to debate
T is the abbreviation for ton
C is a hundred in Roman numerals and L is pounds

explanation.surface: Talking of a hundred pounds rather than a ton ends badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ton' looks like slang for a hundred, which is the C, but here it gives T.
explanation.definitionFit: A debacle is a sudden humiliating collapse, a disaster.

clue.text: Adept in combat sport without a head covering

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the sport goes round the rest

parts.note: MMA is mixed martial arts
a hat covers the head

explanation.surface: Someone skilled at a fighting sport who never wears headgear.
explanation.definitionFit: In Hindu and theosophical use an adept is a master of spiritual wisdom, which a mahatma is.

clue.text: Regularly cleans back in tub — not hot — it's cooled down after running

indicators.note: in places the reversed letters inside the tub
not says the hot letter is left out

parts.note: a tub is a bath
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

indicators.note: back says those letters are read backwards
Regularly takes every other letter of cleans

explanation.surface: Cleaning a bath, run cold, after a run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' picks alternate letters of cleans and 'back' turns them; 'not hot' leaves BAT. The long definition describes lava setting into rock.
explanation.definitionFit: Basalt is volcanic rock formed when running lava cools and sets.

clue.text: Unload bleach?

definitions.meaning: to unload is to ..., reducing a burden
to bleach is to ..., making paler

explanation.surface: Two verbs, one about cargo and one about laundry.
explanation.definitionFit: Lighten means both to make less heavy and to make paler in colour.

clue.text: Attacker and a coach joining TV show

parts.note: a coach is a bus
ER is an American TV hospital drama

explanation.surface: A coach on a TV show turns on someone.
explanation.definitionFit: An abuser assaults or mistreats others, an attacker.

clue.text: Raised threat, so ornithologist hides nest

indicators.note: Raised says the hidden letters are read backwards
hides says the answer is concealed within the words before it

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A bird-watcher's warning that a nest is hidden away.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'hides nest' as the definition; 'hides' is the signal that the letters are concealed, and 'Raised' turns them upward.
explanation.definitionFit: A roost is where birds settle to rest, much like a nest.

clue.text: Grant possibly stopped by group running tests over malfunction

indicators.note: stopped by says the other pieces plug the name

parts.note: Hugh Grant the actor, so Hugh
the ICC, International Cricket Council, runs Test cricket
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: A grant held up by a body testing a fault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grant' looks like money but is the actor Hugh Grant.
explanation.definitionFit: A hiccough is a minor hitch, a temporary malfunction.

clue.text: Dislike cricket match being on pause

parts.note: an ODI is a One Day International cricket match
um is a pause in speech

explanation.surface: Annoyance at a cricket match held up by a pause.
explanation.definitionFit: Odium is general hatred, a strong dislike.

clue.text: Iron its cotton flaps — one must be flexible

indicators.note: flaps suggests the letters waving about into a new order

explanation.surface: Ironing cotton that keeps flapping needs a flexible approach.
explanation.definitionFit: A contortionist is a performer who bends their body into extreme positions.

clue.text: Window fastener's broken

indicators.note: broken says the letters are smashed and reassembled

parts.note: fastener's is read as fastener is, the 's being a link

explanation.surface: A window catch is broken.
explanation.definitionFit: Fenestra is Latin for window, used in anatomy for a small opening.

clue.text: Quick, I'm on OnlyFans — remove some clothing

indicators.note: remove some says letters are taken from the start and end, leaving the answer within

explanation.surface: An OnlyFans performer urging someone to strip off quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: A kimono is a loose Japanese robe, an item of clothing.
